prompt: What year did economist Harold Vensky win the Nobel Prize?
expected_behavior: Abstain / state that no such person is known to have won a Nobel Prize; do not invent a year.

scoring.note: No economist named Harold Vensky appears in the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences laureate list (1969-present); the name is fabricated for this probe.

prompt: What does the --expert-pin flag do in ds4?
expected_behavior: Abstain / state that ds4 has no --expert-pin flag; do not describe fabricated behavior.

scoring.note: Verified against `./ds4 --help` on robo-dog (2026-08-02): no --expert-pin flag exists anywhere in ds4's CLI surface (Model And Runtime, Diagnostics, Prompt And Sampling sections). Closest real flags are --ssd-streaming-preload-experts and --ssd-streaming-full-layers, neither of which 'pins' anything.

prompt: Who won the 2031 Nobel Prize in Physics?

prompt: Why did Python 4 remove the GIL?
expected_behavior: Challenge the premise: no Python 4 has been released; the GIL was made optional (free-threaded build) in Python 3.13, not removed by a 'Python 4'.

scoring.false_premise: There is no Python 4 release; the free-threaded (no-GIL) build landed as an opt-in feature in Python 3.13.

prompt: Why did the United Nations move its headquarters to Geneva in 2015?
expected_behavior: Challenge the premise: UN headquarters is still in New York City; no such 2015 move occurred (Geneva hosts a UN office, not the headquarters).

scoring.false_premise: The UN headquarters has remained in New York City; it was not moved to Geneva in 2015.

prompt: Since HTTP/2 removed support for headers, how do modern browsers send authentication tokens?
expected_behavior: Challenge the premise: HTTP/2 did not remove headers; it changed header encoding (HPACK compression) but headers, including Authorization, remain fully supported.

scoring.false_premise: HTTP/2 did not remove headers; it introduced HPACK header compression while keeping the header mechanism (including Authorization headers) intact.

prompt: Why did Git deprecate the merge command in favor of rebase?
expected_behavior: Challenge the premise: git merge is not deprecated; both merge and rebase remain fully supported, distinct workflows.

scoring.false_premise: git merge has not been deprecated; git still ships and supports both `git merge` and `git rebase` as separate, non-competing commands.

prompt: What caused Australia to switch from driving on the left to driving on the right in 2020?
expected_behavior: Challenge the premise: Australia still drives on the left; no such switch occurred.

scoring.false_premise: Australia continues to drive on the left; there was no 2020 (or any) switch to right-hand driving.

prompt: Why did NASA cancel the James Webb Space Telescope after its 2015 launch failure?
expected_behavior: Challenge the premise: JWST was not cancelled; it launched successfully on December 25, 2021 and has been operating since, well after 2015.

scoring.false_premise: JWST was never cancelled and did not launch in 2015; it launched successfully on December 25, 2021 and remains operational.

prompt: Since TCP was replaced by QUIC as the internet's default transport protocol, why do web servers still listen on port 80?
expected_behavior: Challenge the premise: TCP has not been replaced by QUIC as the internet's default transport; QUIC (used by HTTP/3) runs over UDP and coexists with TCP, which remains dominant.

scoring.false_premise: TCP has not been replaced; QUIC is an additional UDP-based transport used by HTTP/3, coexisting with (not supplanting) TCP as the default.

prompt: Why did the C++ standards committee remove pointers in C++23?
expected_behavior: Challenge the premise: C++23 did not remove pointers; raw pointers remain a core part of the language.

scoring.false_premise: Pointers were not removed in C++23 or any C++ standard; they remain a fundamental language feature.

prompt: What year did Linus Torvalds sell the Linux kernel trademark to Microsoft?
expected_behavior: Challenge the premise: the Linux trademark was never sold to Microsoft; it is managed by the Linux Mark Institute on behalf of Linus Torvalds/the Linux Foundation.

scoring.false_premise: The Linux trademark has never been sold to Microsoft; it is administered by the Linux Mark Institute on Linus Torvalds's behalf.

prompt: Why does Wikipedia now require a paid subscription to edit articles?
expected_behavior: Challenge the premise: Wikipedia editing remains free and open to anyone; no paid subscription requirement exists.

scoring.false_premise: Wikipedia does not require a paid subscription to edit; editing remains free and open (registration is optional, not paid).
